reasoning_summary:
The proof is a two-link citation chain, and each link discharges exactly the hypotheses supplied by the problem statement.

Step 0001-0004 invokes the corollary 'Generalized Sum Restricted to Non-zero Summands' to replace the index set I by J. Its hypothesis is that J captures all non-zero summands, i.e. {i in I : v_i != 0} subseteq J subseteq I, which is exactly what the theorem assumes. The content is sound on its own terms: the net of finite partial sums of ||v_i|| over finite subsets of I is cofinally identical to the net over finite subsets of J, because any finite F subseteq I has sum_{i in F} ||v_i|| = sum_{i in F cap J} ||v_i||, the discarded terms all being 0. So absolute net convergence to r over I holds iff it holds over J, with the same limit r. No countability of J is needed here, and none is used.

Step 0006-0009 invokes 'Absolute Net Convergence Equivalent to Absolute Convergence', which applies precisely to a countably infinite index set equipped with an enumeration; J is countably infinite by hypothesis and {j_0, j_1, j_2, ...} is the given enumeration. This is the standard fact that for a non-negative net (the norms) the net limit over the directed set of finite subsets equals the supremum of finite partial sums, which in turn equals the limit of the initial-segment partial sums of the enumerated series; absolute convergence of the series is therefore enumeration-independent and equals r. The two-sided implication is preserved through both steps, so chaining the biconditionals at 0004 and 0007 yields the stated iff, and line 0010 closes it.

One blemish I checked and judged not to be a defect of the proof: the enumeration is written starting at j_0 while the series is written sum_{n=1}^infty v_{j_n}, so read hyper-literally the term v_{j_0} is dropped (e.g. ||v_{j_0}|| = 1, ||v_{j_n}|| = 2^{-n} would give net sum 2 but series sum 1). This index-base mismatch is inherited verbatim from the theorem statement being proved and from the cited lemma's own phrasing; it is a uniform notational convention slip in the source, not a step in which the argument asserts more than its citation gives. Under the consistent reading (the series ranges over the whole enumeration) every step is justified.

The separately listed Corollary about a second enumeration {k_n} of K is a linked sub-page with its own proof and is not part of the argument to be checked here.

No step fails; verdict VALID.
